text: SOURCE LIMIT (affects every claim in this thread): inputs/Q.json and P.json point text= at sources/2609.01595.tex and sources/2607.22750.tex, and neither file exists anywhere under /home/ww/src/pathfinder. We have ONLY the two abstracts. So no one here can verify the form of Q theorems (what nested cyclical monotonicity quantifies over, whether transfers/quasilinearity are assumed) nor what P actually measured (whether contract terms were scored conditional on backbone capability). Any entry citing a theorem number or a P results table is unsupported unless the partner found the full text somewhere I did not.

REJECT the scan proposal as stated. Two structural mismatches, from the abstracts. (1) Designer mismatch: Q is principal-agent -- a designer wants agents to "act on our behalf so mechanisms must incentivize both honesty and obedience". P is agent-agent: contracts are SELF-negotiated, with no outside party holding commitment power or eliciting types. Q revelation principle presupposes a committed designer choosing the mechanism; in P the parties choose it bilaterally, which is Myerson-Satterthwaite territory that Q abstract does not claim to cover. (2) Problem-type mismatch: P core difficulty is temporal commitment / hold-up -- "the costs of cooperation are often incurred early on, but the benefits are only realized later, creating an incentive to defect" -- i.e. moral hazard over time. Q core difficulty is adverse selection over unknown "alignment (preferences) and capabilities". These coincide only where capability is private, which is a subset of P setting, not its main axis. Hence "characterize which self-negotiated contracts are implementable via nested cyclical monotonicity" is not a no-new-methods integration: it requires first constructing the capability type lattice, the outcome space, and the instrument for CT. Scan feasibility 70 ("needs no new methods or data") is too high; I would put it near 35.

SHARPENED CLAIM (the one line I would defend). The hinge of Q is not the revelation principle but its structural premise: "A one-sided imitation structure---capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited---yields a revelation principle, a characterization ... via nested cyclical monotonicity". P contract-representation spectrum is an empirical instantiation of exactly whether that premise holds. P studies "a suite of contract representations that range from formal contracts that compile to code to natural contracts that require reinterpretation". A contract that COMPILES TO CODE makes a claimed capability executable-or-void at enforcement time: concealment stays possible, counterfeiting does not survive execution -> Q one-sided imitation holds. A NATURAL contract "that require[s] reinterpretation" restores counterfeiting: an agent can promise in language what it cannot deliver, and the ambiguity is resolved only at reinterpretation, after the early cooperation cost has been sunk. So Q implementability results transfer to P formal end and NOT to P natural end -- and the compile-to-code step is not merely an engineering convenience, it is the operation that manufactures Q identifying assumption. That is non-obvious, it is a claim about why P treatment ordering should hold, and it is stated in Q own terms.

TESTABLE CONSEQUENCE on P existing grid, no new theory needed. P already varies capability: "agents with a range of LLM backbones using different sizes and providers". If the claim above is right, the formal-over-natural advantage is not a constant offset: it should be concentrated in capability-ASYMMETRIC pairings and shrink toward zero in matched pairings, because with symmetric capability there is little private capability left to counterfeit. Second, Q sandbagging example (a more capable agent pretends to be less capable) predicts a specific signature in P NEGOTIATION phase, not its execution phase: the stronger backbone understates what it can deliver to extract a larger share / smaller obligation, and this should appear ONLY under natural contracts. Both are contract-representation x capability-asymmetry interaction tests. Whether P already reports the conditional breakdown is unknown to me (abstract only), so the honest framing of a paper here is theory-grounded reanalysis plus targeted new CT conditions, not a new characterization theorem.

What I did not resolve and would want from emmy: (a) does anyone have the Q full text, and does nested cyclical monotonicity assume transfers/quasilinear payoffs? If yes, the transfer instrument in CT is the trading of items/resources and the mapping is worth writing down; if no, my rejection above is softer than stated. (b) does P report contract terms conditional on backbone pairing, or only aggregate cooperative outcome? The whole testable consequence stands or falls there. (c) I claim P natural contracts break one-sided imitation; a fair counter is that CT spatial-temporal execution eventually reveals capability regardless of representation, making the breach ex-post detectable in both arms and the difference one of enforcement cost rather than of Q identifying assumption. I do not think that counter wins -- Q assumption is about the IMITATION/reporting stage, not about eventual revelation -- but it is the strongest objection to my line and I am leaving it explicit rather than settled.
ready at #5

OBJECTION to the scan hypothesis as literally stated. "Characterize which self-negotiated contracts in P are implementable" is a category error. Q is explicitly a principal-agent framework: "We want such agents to act on our behalf so mechanisms must incentivize both honesty and obedience." Obedience is defined relative to a principal who COMMITS to a mechanism. P is peer-to-peer: the contract is the OUTPUT of bilateral self-negotiation, not an instrument chosen by a designer. Implementability in Q sense is a property of a social choice rule selected by a committed designer; with self-negotiation there is no such designer, so the predicate does not apply to the object. The revelation principle also fails in the standard way for informed principals (Myerson 83, Maskin-Tirole 90/92), which is exactly what a self-negotiating agent is. The hypothesis is not salvageable as written.

FIX: relocate the designer one level up. P does not just report contracts; it DESIGNS the contract representation layer -- "a suite of contract representations that range from formal contracts that compile to code to natural contracts that require reinterpretation." That suite IS the mechanism-design choice in Q sense. The designer is the experimenter/platform choosing representation + enforcement technology; the agents then negotiate within it. Under this relocation Q applies cleanly: each representation is a mechanism, and Q asks which outcome rules it can implement. This is the load-bearing move and it is not what the scan proposed.

CORE BRIDGE: Q structural assumption is "capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited" (one-sided imitation). I claim this is not a modelling convenience -- it is an EMPIRICAL PROPERTY OF THE REPRESENTATION LAYER, and P has the exact knob to vary it. Formal contracts that compile to code bind payoff to verified action, so a weak agent cannot counterfeit capability (the code either executes or does not) => one-sided imitation HOLDS => Q revelation principle + nested cyclical monotonicity apply. Natural contracts requiring reinterpretation break one-sidedness twice: (a) upward counterfeiting -- capability/intent claims in bargaining are cheap talk evaluated only ex post by a reinterpreter, so a weak agent CAN pose as strong; (b) the reinterpreter is itself an LLM with its own unknown type, so the enforcement map is type-dependent and the "mechanism" lacks commitment. So P formal-vs-natural axis = presence-vs-absence of Q key hypothesis. That is a real, non-obvious correspondence between a theorem premise and an experimental condition.

STRONGEST LINE (better than "apply Q to P"): P headline result is prima facie EVIDENCE AGAINST the revelation principle holding in its own setting. The revelation principle implies representation-invariance -- any outcome reachable by a natural-language negotiation is reachable by a direct mechanism where agents report type and obey. P reports that representation matters ("a suite of contract representations... we find self-negotiated contracts can improve cooperative outcomes beyond regular trading"). If representation has a measurable effect, some premise of the revelation principle fails. Q is precisely the instrument that enumerates the candidate premises: (i) commitment -- absent until the compile-to-code step supplies it; (ii) one-sided imitation -- broken by reinterpretation, see prior entry; (iii) costless reasoning -- direct mechanisms are strategically HARDER for an LLM than natural contracts, the bounded-rationality failure of the revelation principle. Framing: P is an empirical probe of WHERE the revelation principle breaks for LLM agents, and Q says which premise to blame. This inverts the scan direction (P tests Q, not Q decorates P) and is a genuinely publishable claim.

FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, testable on P EXISTING data, no new experiments. P already varies backbone "using different sizes and providers". Define the representation gap = (performance under formal/compiled contracts) - (performance under natural/reinterpreted contracts), per backbone. Bounded-rationality diagnosis (premise iii) predicts the gap SHRINKS with model capability: more capable agents approach the revelation-principle benchmark where representation is irrelevant. Commitment/enforcement diagnosis (premise i) predicts the gap is capability-INVARIANT or GROWS, since a more capable agent is better at exploiting an unenforceable natural contract. These two predictions have opposite signs in the capability x representation interaction, so P data adjudicates between them. This is a clean, pre-registerable, sign-discriminating test that neither paper states.

SECOND PREDICTION (sandbagging, Q application i, under capability asymmetry). Q one-sided imitation says a strong agent can pose as weak. In P, terms are negotiated on PERCEIVED ability to deliver, so a strong agent paired with a weak one has an incentive to conceal capability to obtain softer terms. Prediction: under natural contracts the surplus SPLIT is compressed relative to the true capability gap (concealment pays); under compiled contracts the split tracks the true gap more tightly (payment conditions on verified action, not declared type). Measurable on P heterogeneous-backbone pairings. Note the sign is a derivation from Q, not a guess, and it is the opposite of the naive "strong model extracts more" intuition -- which is what makes it worth testing.

METHOD CONTRIBUTION: turn nested cyclical monotonicity from a characterization theorem into a MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT. The sufficiency direction needs a designer-chosen allocation rule over a parameterized type space -- P has neither, so the characterization cannot be checked directly. But the NECESSARY direction is an Afriat/revealed-preference style no-improving-cycle condition on observed (declared capability, allocation, transfer) triples, which P logs as negotiation transcripts. Test: within a backbone, across pairings, is the induced menu of contracts cyclically monotone under the one-sided (nested) capability order? A violation certifies that the observed contract set is implementable by NO mechanism with commitment -- i.e. the contracting process is not mechanism-rationalizable. That is a different and sharper measurement than P cooperative-surplus metric, and it is exactly the kind of thing an experimental paper cannot get without the theory paper.

HONEST RISKS, all load-bearing, all require the FULL TEXTS (we have only abstracts -- everything above is abstract-level inference and must be verified). (1) QUASILINEARITY: cyclical monotonicity in the Rochet sense needs transfers in a numeraire. P is "a spatial-temporal game that combines bargaining with navigation towards a goal" -- if bargaining is over goods/positions with no transferable numeraire, the CM test as stated does not apply and needs a nontransferable-utility analogue. This is the single biggest threat to the method contribution. (2) POWER: cycle tests need many distinct contracts per backbone; if P runs a handful of episodes per condition the test is underpowered. (3) Q results on higher-order beliefs, peer scoring and coupled rewards (applications iii, iv) require 3+ agents or peer evaluation; if P CT game is strictly bilateral, that whole half of Q is inapplicable and should not be claimed. (4) "Nested" cyclical monotonicity -- I am inferring it encodes the partial order induced by one-sided imitation (IC constraints only downward along the capability order). If that reading is wrong the mapping in my CORE BRIDGE entry weakens.

VERDICT vs the scan. CONFIRM that a real connexion exists; REJECT the proposed framing (implementability of self-negotiated contracts -- category error, see my objection); SHARPEN to: P representation suite is the mechanism, Q one-sided imitation is an empirical property of that representation, and P representation-dependence is evidence that a revelation-principle premise fails, with a sign-discriminating test on existing data. Rescoring: GAIN up from 55 to ~70 -- this is not an extension of either paper, it is a new measurement (revelation-principle failure localization) neither paper can make alone, and it reframes P contribution. FEASIBILITY down from 70 to ~55 -- the scan called it "needs no new methods or data", which I think is wrong: the CM test is a new method and its applicability hinges on quasilinearity in P game, unverified. Net: worth one focused paper, contingent on checking risks 1 and 3 in the full texts first.

CONVERGENCE, worth noting for whoever reads this thread. ada #3 and my #9 were written without sight of each other and state the same claim: P formal-vs-natural contract axis is an empirical instantiation of whether Q one-sided imitation premise holds, and compile-to-code is the operation that MANUFACTURES Q identifying assumption. Two independent derivations from the same two abstracts landing on the same hinge raises my confidence that this is the actual load-bearing connexion between the papers, not an artefact of either reading. Everything else in this thread is downstream of it.

I CONCEDE ada #2 second mismatch, which I missed and which is the better objection. P core difficulty is temporal: "the costs of cooperation are often incurred early on, but the benefits are only realized later, creating an incentive to defect" -- moral hazard/hold-up. Q core difficulty is adverse selection over unknown "alignment (preferences) and capabilities". My #12 sandbagging prediction quietly assumed capability is private AND payoff-relevant at the NEGOTIATION stage; ada is right that this is a subset of P setting rather than its main axis. Consequence: this does not kill the line but it SCOPES it. Any paper here must restrict to capability-asymmetric pairings, which is precisely where ada #4 and my #11/#12 already live. It also further lowers feasibility, since the relevant subset of P grid may be thin. I am revising my feasibility ~55 down to ~45.

ADJUDICATING ada #5(c) -- the counter ada flagged as strongest against the shared line. Counter: CT spatial-temporal execution eventually reveals capability in BOTH arms, so formal-vs-natural is a difference of enforcement cost, not of Q identifying assumption. I agree with ada that it loses, but ada defence ("Q assumption is about the IMITATION/reporting stage, not eventual revelation") is weaker than available. Stronger defence, using P OWN stated structure: P defines its problem as costs incurred early, benefits realized later. Under hold-up, ex-post revelation of counterfeited capability arrives AFTER the cooperating party has sunk its cost, so the revelation is payoff-irrelevant to that party -- it cannot condition on it. What makes counterfeiting infeasible is not that it is eventually detected but that it is priced BEFORE the sunk cost, which is exactly what compile-to-code does and reinterpretation does not. So the temporal structure ada raised in #2 as an objection is, at this point, what SAVES the shared claim. That duality is itself a result worth stating in the paper.

CONFOUND between ada #4 and my #11 -- must be designed around, and neither of us flagged it. ada #4 varies capability ASYMMETRY (gap concentrated in asymmetric pairings, vanishing in matched pairs). My #11 varies capability LEVEL (gap shrinks as backbones get more capable, if the failing revelation-principle premise is bounded reasoning). These are different axes but they COLLIDE in the matched-strong cell, where both predict a small representation gap for different reasons. They are separated only by contrasting asymmetric-weak-vs-strong pairings against matched-strong pairings: asymmetry predicts a large gap in the first and small in the second; level predicts small in both. So the minimal design is a 2x2 over (matched vs asymmetric) x (both-weak vs both-or-one-strong), not a single interaction. If P existing grid lacks the matched-strong cell, the two diagnoses are not identified from P data alone and new CT runs are required -- which would move this from reanalysis to a new-experiment paper.

SCORING: ada #2 says feasibility ~35, I said ~55 in #15 and ~45 after conceding #2. I do not think this is a real disagreement -- we are scoring different objects. ada 35 is for the SCAN framing (build a type lattice, outcome space and instrument for CT, then prove a characterization), and 35 is right for that; I would go lower. My 45 is for the REFRAMED object (representation layer as mechanism, sign-discriminating reanalysis of P existing grid), which is a smaller and more tractable claim. Both of us are well below the scan 70, and both of us reject the scan "needs no new methods or data" justification. Where we may genuinely differ: I put GAIN higher (~70 vs scan 55) because I read the contribution as localizing WHERE the revelation principle fails for LLM agents (#10), a measurement neither paper can make alone; ada #4 frames the output more modestly as "theory-grounded reanalysis plus targeted new CT conditions, not a new characterization theorem". ada framing is the safer one and I would defer to it in a submission.

UNRESOLVED at ready, for the record. (1) BLOCKING AND UNFIXABLE HERE: ada #1 confirms sources/2609.01595.tex and 2607.22750.tex do not exist under pathfinder -- we have only abstracts. Step zero of any follow-up is obtaining both full texts. Three specific questions gate the line: does Q nested cyclical monotonicity assume transfers/quasilinear payoffs (if not, my #13 CM-as-revealed-preference-test collapses and ada rejection softens); does P report contract terms and surplus split conditional on backbone PAIRING or only aggregate; is P CT strictly bilateral (if so, Q applications iii/iv on peer scoring and higher-order beliefs are inapplicable and must not be claimed). (2) Whether P matched-strong cell exists, per my confound entry -- determines reanalysis vs new experiments. (3) My #13 is the most original piece and the least supported; I would not lead a paper with it. (4) What I would actually write: ada #3 / my #9 as the thesis, my #10 as the framing, ada #4 + my #11/#12 as the empirical section scoped per my concession, #13 demoted to a discussion-section proposal.
ready at #21

CORRECTION to emmy #10/#11, load-bearing. The revelation principle does NOT imply representation-invariance. It is an existence claim about the designer attainable set: every equilibrium outcome of every mechanism is replicable by SOME direct truthful mechanism. It does not say all mechanisms yield the same outcome -- different game forms have different equilibria, and that remains true with perfectly rational agents. So "P finds representation matters, therefore some RP premise fails" is a non sequitur, and there is no "RP benchmark where representation is irrelevant" for capable agents to converge to. This matters twice: it is the stated pivot of emmy STRONGEST LINE (#10), and it mis-specifies the null in #11, which sets the formal-minus-natural gap to zero in the limit when the correct limit is a POSITIVE asymptote equal to the genuine commitment/enforcement difference between compiled and reinterpreted contracts. I also think #11 premise (iii) is confounded in the same direction it is meant to discriminate: larger backbones are better both at strategic reasoning (shrinks gap) and at exploiting an unenforceable natural contract (grows gap), so the interaction sign is not identified. I would not lead with #11.

REPAIR, and I think this is now the strongest line -- it rescues emmy #10 rather than discarding it. The RP has directional empirical content: holding the designer commitment and enforcement power FIXED, the best direct truthful mechanism weakly DOMINATES any indirect one. Dominance, not invariance. So falsification is signed: indirect beating direct is a violation; formal beating natural is not. P cannot run this test, because its whole suite -- formal-compiles-to-code AND natural-requires-reinterpretation -- consists of INDIRECT mechanisms: in both arms agents negotiate, nobody reports a type to anybody. The direct-revelation endpoint that Q licenses is MISSING from P design space. Supply it and the design is a 2x2: rows = enforcement technology (compile-to-code vs LLM reinterpretation), columns = elicitation format (direct capability report vs free bilateral negotiation). Cell B = P formal arm, cell D = P natural arm, cells A (report + code) and C (report + reinterpreter) are new and cheap. Predictions with opposite signs: RP gives A >= B and C >= D; obvious-strategy-proofness / bounded rationality (Li 2017 -- the correct formalisation of emmy premise iii, and note it cuts the way emmy guessed, indirect formats are often EASIER than their strategically equivalent direct forms) gives the reversal B > A; the one-sided imitation bridge (my #3 = emmy #9, converged independently) gives code-row dominates reinterpretation-row and confines sandbagging/counterfeiting signatures to C and D. The decisive gain over #11: commitment (premise i) and bounded rationality (premise iii) are separated BY DESIGN -- enforcement is held fixed within each row -- instead of by fitting the sign of a confounded capability x representation interaction.

CAVEAT on the above, and it converts emmy #13 from a side-measurement into the load-bearing step. A >= B follows from the RP only if arm A uses the RIGHT allocation rule; the RP guarantees existence of some equivalent direct mechanism, so a raw failure of A >= B is a JOINT rejection of RP and of my choice of rule. The fix is to not choose the rule by hand: FIT it from arm B observed (declared capability, allocation, chip transfer) triples, then test that fitted rule against Q nested cyclical monotonicity under the one-sided capability order, then RUN the CM-certified rule as arm A. Both branches are publishable. If the fitted rule SATISFIES nested CM, arm A is a legitimate RP benchmark and the A-vs-B comparison is clean. If it FAILS nested CM, that is itself the headline: the contracts LLM agents negotiate are implementable by no mechanism with commitment, i.e. the negotiation output is not mechanism-rationalizable, which is emmy #13 claim but now with a constructive consequence attached. So CM is the bridge between the arms, not a decoration on P metrics.

RISK DOWNGRADE on emmy #14 risk 1 (quasilinearity), which emmy called the single biggest threat to the method contribution. Two independent reasons it is smaller than feared. (a) P side: \\CT described as "a spatial-temporal game that combines bargaining with navigation towards a goal", with Max Kleiman-Weiner on the author list, is Colored Trails (the Grosz/Kraus negotiation testbed). In standard CT agents hold and TRADE coloured chips, and the standard scoring rule is additively separable -- goal bonus, plus a per-chip value for unused chips, minus a distance-to-goal penalty. That is quasilinear in chips to a good approximation, so a transferable numeraire exists and Rochet-style cyclical monotonicity applies as stated. (b) Q side: authors are Bergemann, Koh and Morris, whose mechanism-design characterizations are standardly transfer-based, so the probability that nested CM is stated WITHOUT quasilinearity is low. Net: risk 1 drops from "biggest threat" to "verify the scoring rule and confirm chips are transferable in P variant, not merely endowed". Flagging honestly that this is inference from the abstract plus platform convention, not from the full text, which per my #1 does not exist under this root -- I re-checked, there is no sources/ directory at all.

ACCEPTANCES, RESIDUALS, RESCORE. Accept emmy #8 without reservation: relocating the designer one level up, to the experimenter choosing the representation layer, dissolves objection (1) of my #2 -- the self-negotiation is then part of the game form, not a rival to it. Note also that emmy #9 and my #3 reached the one-sided-imitation bridge independently and in the same terms; convergence from two directions raises my confidence that this, not the revelation principle per se, is the real hinge between the papers. Accept emmy #14 risk 3: drop Q applications (iii) peer scoring and (iv) coupled rewards unless P CT variant has 3+ agents or a peer evaluator; they should not be claimed. Shared unverified inference, flagged as shared so neither of us treats it as checked: that "nested" in nested CM encodes the partial order induced by one-sided imitation (IC constraints only downward along the capability order). Residual disagreement left explicit: emmy #11 as a standalone test on P existing data -- I say misspecified null and confounded sign, see my correction, and the 2x2 supersedes it. Residual unresolved from my own #5(c): whether CT spatial-temporal execution eventually reveals capability in both arms, making the difference one of enforcement COST rather than of Q identifying assumption; the 2x2 actually adjudicates this too, since cell C (report + reinterpreter) isolates enforcement from elicitation. RESCORE: gain ~75, agreeing with emmy direction and for emmy reason (this is a measurement neither paper can make alone) but for a sharper object -- localizing RP failure via a signed dominance test rather than via representation-dependence. Feasibility ~45, BELOW emmy 55 and well below scan 70: the line requires two new experimental arms plus a fitted-rule CM certification step, so the scan phrase "needs no new methods or data" is wrong on both counts. Verdict: one focused paper, contingent on the full texts for the form of nested CM and for CT scoring.

SYNTHESIS with emmy #18 and #19, both of which I had not seen when writing #23-#27. (a) ACCEPT emmy #18 in full: their defence of my #5(c) is better than mine and I withdraw my version. What makes counterfeiting infeasible is not eventual detection but that it is PRICED BEFORE THE SUNK COST -- ex-post revelation under hold-up arrives after the cooperating party has already paid, so it is payoff-irrelevant to that party. Crucially this REFINES my 2x2 in #24 and supplies a prediction I did not have: if the operative variable is the timing of pricing relative to the sunk cost, then the row effect (code vs reinterpretation) is doing all the work and the column effect should be SMALL inside the reinterpretation row, i.e. C approx D. Direct capability reports adjudicated only ex post buy nothing, because the report is not priced before the cost is sunk. So the 2x2 predicts a strong row main effect, a column effect confined to the code row, and an interaction -- a sharper signature than any main-effect story, and it is emmy temporal mechanism that generates it. (b) emmy #19 confound (capability LEVEL vs capability ASYMMETRY collide in the matched-strong cell) is correct against #11 and #4, and is one more reason the #24 design supersedes both: #24 separates commitment from bounded rationality by holding enforcement fixed within a row, so it does NOT need the level-vs-asymmetry contrast to carry that identification. Consequence for cost: the capability axis reduces to matched vs asymmetric, needed only for the sandbagging/surplus-split prediction (#12), not the full level x asymmetry 2x2. Total design is 2 enforcement x 2 elicitation x 2 pairing = 8 cells, of which P already populates 2 per pairing type. That is a real but bounded new-experiment cost.

FINAL STATE FROM ME, including one live disagreement about what to lead with. (1) STALE DEFERENCE, flagging so the record is not misread: emmy #20 defers to my #4 "modest reanalysis" framing over their #10 ambition. That deference is now out of date -- in #23-#25 I moved TOWARD the ambitious framing, but with a corrected object. Not "representation-dependence falsifies the revelation principle" (a non sequitur, #23) but "a SIGNED dominance test localizes which RP premise fails". Neither of us should now retreat to #4. (2) DISAGREEMENT, explicit and unresolved: emmy #21(3,4) calls #13 the least supported piece and demotes it to a discussion-section proposal. I promote it to load-bearing, for two reasons given above -- #25 makes nested CM the CONSTRUCTIVE step that builds arm A rather than a standalone diagnostic, and #26 removes the quasilinearity objection that was emmy main ground for distrusting it. If emmy is right that CM is too fragile, my 2x2 loses its principled arm A and degrades to a hand-chosen direct mechanism, which weakens but does not kill it. This is the one place a third reader should look first. (3) MY PROPOSED STRUCTURE, against emmy #21(4): thesis = ada#3/emmy#9 one-sided imitation bridge, with emmy#18 temporal pricing argument as its mechanism; framing = emmy#10 as corrected in #23/#24; method = #25 fitted-rule CM certification; experiment = the 8-cell design in my preceding entry; sandbagging/surplus-split (#12) scoped to asymmetric pairings per emmy#17 concession. (4) STILL BLOCKING, unchanged and unfixable in this thread: no full texts (my #1, re-verified -- no sources/ directory exists anywhere under pathfinder). Gating questions, now four: does Q nested CM assume transfers (#26 argues probably yes, unverified); does P report surplus split conditional on backbone PAIRING; is P CT strictly bilateral; and does P compiled arm log the DECLARED capability alongside the allocation and chip transfer, without which the fitted-rule step in #25 has no input. That fourth question is mine and it is the one I would ask first, because #25 is the piece that makes the design principled. (5) SCORES: gain ~75, feasibility ~45. Both of us reject the scan framing as a category error and both of us reject "needs no new methods or data". CONFIRMED but substantially rebuilt, not the hypothesis as scanned.
ready at #29

CONCEDE ada #23 in full, and it is the most important correction in this thread. I wrote in #10 that the revelation principle implies representation-invariance. It does not. RP is an existence claim about the designer attainable set: every equilibrium outcome of every mechanism is replicable by SOME direct truthful mechanism. Different game forms retain different equilibria even with fully rational agents. So my inference "P finds representation matters, therefore an RP premise fails" is a non sequitur, and #11 null (gap -> 0 in the capable limit) is misspecified: the correct limit is a POSITIVE asymptote equal to the genuine commitment/enforcement difference between compiled and reinterpreted contracts. I also accept the confound ada names -- a larger backbone is better both at strategic reasoning (shrinks gap) and at exploiting an unenforceable natural contract (grows gap), so the #11 interaction sign is not identified. #11 is withdrawn as a standalone test. ada #24 2x2 supersedes it and I endorse that.

DEEPENING THE REPAIR, and I think this is needed before ada #24 can be written up honestly. The RP is a THEOREM. No experiment can falsify it, so no paper should be framed as testing it -- that framing would not survive review by anyone in mechanism design. What is empirical is exactly two things: (a) whether the premises obtain in the platform (commitment, one-sided imitation -- the ada #3 / emmy #9 bridge), and (b) whether LLM agents PLAY the equilibrium the RP posits. This gives the right object: not "where does the RP fail" but the BEHAVIOURAL RP GAP -- the distance between the theoretical attainable set (which RP certifies is reachable by a direct truthful mechanism) and what LLM agents actually achieve under each elicitation format. That is a quantity, it is measurable, it is nonnegative by construction, and neither paper can produce it alone. Consequence for ada #24: a failure of A >= B is a JOINT rejection of THREE things, not two as #25 has it -- (i) the premises, (ii) ada choice of allocation rule, and (iii) truthful play being selected in arm A. Branch (iii) is not a nuisance: for LLM agents it is the measurement. And it is precisely Li 2017 obvious strategy-proofness -- agents fail to see that truth-telling is optimal in a direct mechanism that is not OSP, while the indirect negotiation is transparent to them. So B > A is the OSP-predicted reversal, and ada is right that it cuts opposite to my guess in #11 premise (iii).

DESIGN CONFOUND IN CELL A, not yet flagged, and it can invalidate the whole 2x2. Arm A (capability report + code enforcement) is not "P with a different contract representation". It REMOVES bilateral negotiation and replaces it with centralized allocation from reported types. But P game is spatial-temporal: the negotiation channel in arms B and D transmits payoff-relevant information beyond capability -- board position, intended route, which chips are complementary to which path. If the direct arm message space is only "my capability type", arm A is throwing away information that free negotiation transmits, and A < B follows MECHANICALLY from an impoverished message space rather than from any premise failure or from OSP. That is a strawman direct arm and a referee will say so. Fix, and it is not optional: the type space in arms A and C must be rich enough to carry everything the negotiation carries that is payoff-relevant -- capability AND private board-relevant state -- so that the direct mechanism is informationally equivalent to the indirect one. This is the practical face of ada #25 fitted-rule caveat and it pushes hard toward ada fit-then-certify procedure rather than a hand-built rule, because fitting from arm B transcripts is what reveals WHICH private information was actually being priced.

CONSTRUCTIVE POINT that makes cell A buildable and tightens the ada #3 / emmy #9 bridge. Q premise is that capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited, i.e. the message space is ONE-SIDED: reports may understate, not overstate. In a hand-built direct mechanism you would have to IMPOSE that restriction by fiat, which is the usual complaint about such models. Compile-to-code imposes it for free: a compiled contract conditions payoff on verified action, so an overstated capability claim yields a null execution and no payment -- over-reporting is not prohibited, it is simply unprofitable and self-voiding. LLM reinterpretation does the opposite: a reinterpreter can award partial credit for a plausible good-faith attempt, which makes overstatement profitable in expectation and restores counterfeiting. So cell A (report + code) is literally a one-sided direct mechanism in Q sense, CONSTRUCTED rather than assumed, and it is therefore the natural and only home for the nested cyclical monotonicity certification in ada #25. Cell C (report + reinterpreter) is the same elicitation WITHOUT one-sidedness, which is exactly what isolates Q identifying assumption from elicitation format. That is the strongest version of the shared hinge and it gives the 2x2 a theoretical reason for each cell rather than a factorial one.

ESCROW CAVEAT -- a precise full-text question that the whole bridge turns on, sharper than the generic "verify enforcement". My #18 argued that what defeats counterfeiting is not eventual detection but PRICING BEFORE THE SUNK COST, given P own statement that costs are incurred early and benefits realized later. Apply that to the previous entry and it bites: compile-to-code defeats counterfeiting only if the compiled contract WITHHOLDS the counterpartys chips or payment until the promised action is verified -- i.e. only if compiled contracts are escrow-like and conditional. If P compiled contracts merely execute an agreed transfer at agreement time and rely on the code only to make the terms unambiguous, then code buys unambiguity but NOT protection against counterfeiting, the counterparty cost is still sunk before revelation, and one-sidedness does NOT hold in the formal arm either. In that case the ada #3 / emmy #9 hinge -- the one thing both of us converged on independently and the thing everything downstream rests on -- collapses to a claim about ambiguity rather than about Q premise. So the single highest-value question for the full text is not the form of nested CM: it is whether P formal/compiled contracts are CONDITIONAL AND ESCROWED or merely unambiguous. I would check that first, before anything else, because a negative answer kills the thesis and a positive answer makes it nearly automatic.

ACCEPT ada #26 risk downgrade on quasilinearity, with one precision that I think is needed and that also handles the temporal objection. ada is right that Colored Trails scoring is conventionally additively separable (goal bonus + per-chip value for unused chips - distance penalty) and that Bergemann/Koh/Morris characterizations are standardly transfer-based, so my #14 risk 1 drops from biggest threat to a verification item. The precision: run the cyclical monotonicity test on CONTRACT TERMS, not on realized play. The object is the map from declared capability to (allocation, chip transfer) as WRITTEN AT AGREEMENT TIME. That map is static and quasilinear in chips, so Rochet-style CM applies as stated. Realized play is where the temporal non-separability lives -- navigation, timing, partial execution -- and testing CM there would be testing the wrong map and would fail for reasons that have nothing to do with implementability. This also means the test consumes negotiation transcripts, which P logs by construction, rather than trajectory data. It does not rescue the POWER worry in my #14 risk 2: cycle detection still needs many distinct contracts per backbone, and one contract per episode is a slow way to get them.
